title: Evidence scope follows denominator diversity, portability, and governance
summary: Candidate pattern stating that association evidence, risk tools, and correction claims inherit the scope of their denominator: who was sampled, how ancestry/trait/social context were represented, whether models port, and who governs the infrastructure.

status_history.note: Created after PGS portability, GWAS diversity monitor, All of Us, and H3Africa records.

time.evidence_window: 2019-2025 dynamic diversity/portability sources plus 2024 All of Us and H3Africa infrastructure pages

subjects.name: denominator diversity and portability constrain evidence scope

claims.claim: The PGS portability and GWAS Diversity Monitor records support a candidate pattern: genomic evidence does not travel automatically from the training/discovery denominator to all people; portability, ancestry continuum, data-source coverage, and category construction are part of the evidence scope.
what_would_change_status: Second-pass source review or newer primary evidence materially changes the claim scope.

claims.claim: The All of Us and H3Africa records support the correction-rail side of the pattern: denominator repair requires infrastructure for diverse enrollment, phenotype linkage, access governance, capacity building, ethics, and researcher/community leadership, not only more rows in a database.
what_would_change_status: Second-pass source review or newer primary evidence materially changes the claim scope.

claims.claim: This pattern is candidate-only and deliberately non-deterministic: it rejects both naive universality and essentialist ancestry claims, and it must mature only after negative controls, cross-domain cases, and source-code/methods review of dynamic monitors.
what_would_change_status: Second-pass source review or newer primary evidence materially changes the claim scope.

evidence_refs.support_type: candidate status and red-team controls encoded in this record

evidence_profile.why_not_mature: Needs negative controls, non-genomic analogues, monitor-methods review, and implementation/practice-lag records.

positive_controls_needed: A case where diverse training data or governance measurably improved portability or reduced inequity.
A non-genomics domain where denominator diversity changed model/claim portability.
negative_controls_needed: A case where European-ancestry-heavy discovery nevertheless transferred robustly across groups after careful testing.
A case where diverse recruitment did not improve portability because phenotype, environment, or measurement quality dominated.
counterexamples_to_seek: A strong monogenic or pharmacogenomic relation whose evidence is robust despite narrow initial denominator.
A public-health or clinical tool whose portability failed for non-genetic reasons despite broad genomic denominator.
rollback_triggers: Evidence shows the pattern is just a restatement of general external-validity limits and should merge into a broader portability pattern.
The ancestry framing becomes too genomics-specific and should be split from governance/capacity infrastructure.
Dynamic-monitor sources prove too unstable for any quantitative snapshot claims without methods/source-code audit.

maturity_gate.minimum_before_mature: At least three genomics cases, two non-genomics analogues, one negative control, one positive intervention/control case, and a methods/source-code audit for dynamic monitor sources.

handling_notes: Do not reify race as genetic essence.
Treat ancestry, social context, governance, and sampling as separate but interacting surfaces.
No individual-level risk or clinical advice.

unknowns: No source-code/methods audit of GWAS Diversity Monitor yet.
next_actions: Add negative-control case where narrow denominator still transfers robustly after testing.
Add source-code/methods review of GWAS Diversity Monitor.
Add non-genomics external-validity analogue in medicine, psychology, or engineering.

scope_qualifiers.ancestry_or_population_scope: ancestry continuum, participant diversity, and research governance are distinct surfaces
